historical_references.reference: According to legend, Saint Nataliana was a Greek maiden who was martyred during the Roman persecutions of Christians. She was said to have been a beautiful and virtuous young woman who lived in the city of Thessalonica. When the Roman governor, Dionysius, demanded that she offer sacrifices to the pagan gods, she refused, and was sentenced to death. She was taken to the place of execution, and as she was being led to the stake, a miraculous event occurred: a bear appeared and attacked the executioners, allowing Nataliana to escape. She was later captured and brought before the governor again, but the earth opened up and swallowed her, taking her to heaven. Nataliana is venerated as the patron saint of those involved in agriculture and animals.

Saint Natalia of Rome, also known as Saint Nataliana, was a Christian martyr who lived in the late 1st or early 2nd century AD. According to tradition, she was a noblewoman from Rome who was married to a pagan soldier named Publius. After Publius was killed in battle, Natalia was approached by a group of Christian missionaries who asked her to convert to their faith. She was initially reluctant, but eventually agreed and was baptized. However, her conversion was not kept a secret for long, and she was denounced to the Roman authorities by her former servants. She was imprisoned and subjected to various tortures, but remained steadfast in her faith. She was eventually sentenced to death and was executed by being buried alive. Natalia is venerated as the patron saint of those who are persecuted for their faith and those who experience difficulties in marriage.
